GANG SPECIAL RULES

Ghosts of the Wastes: At the start of the battle, before the first roll for Priority, two Ash Waste Nomad Fighters may swap positions on the battlefield. Additionally, Ash Waste Nomad Fighters ignore both difficult and dangerous terrain.

Natives of the Wastes: An Ash Waste Nomad gang may not include any Vehicles or Mounts that are not included in their Equipment List.

Starting Skills: When added to a Gang Roster, all Ash Waste Nomad Leaders and Champions may select one skill from one of their Primary Skill Sets.

Skill Access: This gang’s Fighters have access to the following Skill Sets:

140 credits

Fighter (Champion) Starting XP: 49

MWSBSSTWIASvLdClWilInt
5”3+4+332425+6887

Call the Storm: While equipped with a Stormcaller staff, an Active Ash Waste Nomad Stormcaller can perform the Dust Storm action:

Dust Storm (Single): If the Visibility (X”) rule is not active for this battle, apply the Visibility (24”) rule. Otherwise, either increase or decrease the value of X” by 6” to a minimum of 6”. These effects last for the remainder of the battle and can be modified further by future uses of this ability.

Equipment: An Ash Waste Nomad Stormcaller is equipped with a Dustback Helamite (included in their cost) and, when added to a Gang Roster, may purchase weapons and wargear from the Ash Waste Nomad Equipment List:

• During the course of a campaign, they may be given additional weapons and wargear purchased from the Ash Waste Nomad List and from the Trading Post.

ARTHROMITE DUNESKUTTLER

225 credits

Fighter (Beast, Brute) Starting XP: 25

MWSBSSTWIASvLdClWilInt
6”3+5+553444+7864

Hard to Kill: An Arthromite Duneskuttler is notoriously hard to kill; when rolling on the Lasting Injury table for an Arthromite Duneskuttler, roll twice and apply whichever result the owning player wishes.

Skills: An Arthromite Duneskuttler has the Clamber skill.

Equipment: An Arthromite Duneskuttler is armed with mandibles. They may not purchase or be equipped with additional weapons or wargear.

ARTHROMITE SPINEWYRM

60 credits

Fighter (Beast, Pet) Starting XP: 13

MWSBSSTWIASvLdClWilInt
6”4+6+231416+6764

Leash Range: An Arthromite Spinewyrm has a 6” Leash range.

Small Target: Arthromite Spinewyrms are low to the ground and surprisingly fast, making them difficult to target in the vast expanse of the ash wastes. Ranged attacks against Arthromite Spinewyrms are made at -1 to Hit.

Burrowing: An Arthromite Spinewyrm is able to burrow beneath and through the metal and rockcrete floors of the underhive, passing quickly through hidden crawl spaces and buried vents, before emerging elsewhere. An Arthromite Spinewyrm may move freely under impassable terrain if it has sufficient movement to do so, but may not end its movement on or with impassable terrain.

Equipment: An Arthromite Spinewyrm is armed with barbed fangs. They may not purchase or be equipped with additional weapons or wargear.

UNBOUND HELAMITE

70 credits

Fighter (Beast, Pet) Starting XP: 13

MWSBSSTWIASvLdClWilInt
8”5+6+331416+6774

Leash Range: An Unbound Helamite has a 3” Leash range.

Spare Mount: If an Unbound Helamite’s owner is equipped with a Dustback Helamite and is Suppressed whilst within 1” of an Active Unbound Helamite, they may make an Agility test. If the test is passed, the Unbound Helamite changes its Status to Suppressed instead of its owner.

Equipment: An Unbound Helamite is armed with Helamite claws. They may not purchase or be equipped with additional weapons or wargear.

ASHWING HELAMITE

70 credits

Fighter (Beast, Flying, Pet) Starting XP: 13

MWSBSSTWIASvLdClWilInt
8”4+6+231516+6564

Leash Range: An Ashwing Helamite has a 9” Leash range.

Ashwing Lure: While Active, an Ashwing Helamite’s owner may perform the Deploy Lure action:

• Deploy Lure (Single): Place an Ashwing Lure in base contact with this Fighter. For the remainder of the battle, the lure is treated as terrain and any Ashwing Helamites this Fighter controls treat the Ashwing Lure as if it were their owner. Any Fighter can perform the Interact action while within 1” of the Ashwing Lure in order to move a distance equal to their Movement characteristic and place the Ashwing Lure in base contact with the Fighter at the end of this move.

Equipment: An Ashwing Helamite is armed with toxic mandibles. They may not purchase or be equipped with additional weapons or wargear.

WARGEAR

ARMOUR & FIELD ARMOUR

  • Mesh armour40 cr

    40 CREDITS – TP 0

    A Fighter equipped with mesh armour increases their Save characteristic by 1 when resolving Hits suffered in close combat.

  • Refractor field50 cr

    50 CREDITS – TP 2

    A refractor field grants its wearer a 5+ Invulnerable save; however, should a natural 1 be rolled when making the Invulnerable save then the refractor field is burned out and cannot be used again for the rest of the battle.

    A refractor field may be combined with other armour and field armour.

GANG SPECIAL RULES

Blessed by the Chaos Gods: Chaos Helot cults can perform Chaos Rituals (see below).

Starting Skills: When added to a Gang Roster, all Chaos Helot Leaders and Champions may select one skill from one of their Primary Skill Sets.

Skill Access: This gang’s Fighters have access to the following Skill Sets:

FighterAgilityBrawnCombatCunningSavantShooting
Cult Demagogue-PrimarySecondarySecondaryPrimary-
Cult Disciple-Secondary-PrimarySecondaryPrimary
Cult WitchSecondary--PrimaryPrimary-
Cultist--PrimarySecondary-Secondary
InitiateSecondary--Primary--
Chaos FamiliarPrimary--Secondary--
Chaos SpawnSecondaryPrimary-Secondary--

CHAOS RITUALS

The following Post-cycle Action are available to Chaos Helot cults and Chaos Corrupted gangs:

LEAD RITUAL (LEADER ONLY

Select which of the Chaos gods the ritual is attempting to invoke: the Blood God, the Plague Lord, the Dark Prince or the Architect of Fate (note: a Chaos Corrupted gang can only attempt to invoke the Chaos god they have dedicated themselves to).

Roll 2D6 and apply the following modifiers:

  • +1 if the gang won a battle this Campaign Cycle.
  • +1 if the gang gained Reputation this Campaign Cycle.
  • +2 if the cult already has the favour of the god the ritual is invoking marked on their Gang Roster.
  • - 2 if the cult has the favour of a different god to the one the ritual is invoking marked on their Gang Roster.
  • - 1 if the gang lost a battle this Campaign Cycle.
  • - 1 if the gang lost Reputation this Campaign Cycle.

If the final result is 9 or more, the ritual is heeded by the cult’s patron. Mark on their Gang Roster that they have the favour of their chosen god – the effects of this favour are listed as follows. If they already have the favour of a different god, it is replaced. In addition, if another Fighter perform the Ritual Focus Post-cycle Action, they immediately gain D3+3 XP.

If, however, the final result is a natural double 1, or is 2 or less after modifiers, the cult is deemed unworthy. They lose any favour they had with the gods. Furthermore, if another Fighter performed the Ritual Focus Post-cycle Action, they are turned into a Chaos Spawn – remove the Fighter from the Gang Roster and add a Chaos Spawn to the Gang Roster.

RITUAL FOCUS (MAX ONE FIGHTER)

The Fighter offers themselves to be the focus of the Chaos Ritual. This may have additional effects on the Fighter as described in the Lead Ritual Post-cycle Action.

THE GOD’S FAVOUR

If the gang has successfully performed a Chaos Ritual and has marked on their Gang Roster the favour of their chosen god, the appropriate bonus is gained during the gang’s next battle:

The Blood God: Once per round, a single failed Wound roll can be re-rolled.

The Plague Lord: Once per round, a single Recovery roll can be re-rolled.

The Dark Prince: Once per round, during the Activation phase, two models that are Ready can be picked and activated one after the other, rather than the usual one.

Neither of these models may perform the Group Activation action.

The Architect of Fate: Once per round, a single Hit roll can be re-rolled.

Leash Range: A Chaos Familiar has a 3” Leash range.

Omen of Fortune: A Chaos Familiar is able to sense bad fortune and forewarn its companion, giving them a flash of precognition. While they are within Leash range of their owner, their owner has a 4+ Invulnerable save.

Precognition: The gift of foresight possessed by the Chaos Familiar enables it to dodge and evade all but the most unexpected of attacks. This tremendous precognition grants them a 4+ Invulnerable save.

Psychic Manifestation: A Chaos Familiar is an extension of the owner’s will and a clear indication of the favour the gods of Chaos have bestowed upon them. If the owning Fighter has the Wyrd Subtype, once per round they may re-roll a failed Willpower check to manifest a Wyrd Power.

Skills: A Chaos Familiar has the Clamber skill.

Random Movement: The Movement characteristic for a Chaos Spawn is random; roll each time the Chaos Spawn is activated.

Blessed by the Chaos Gods: When a Chaos Spawn is taken Out of Action, do not roll on the Lasting Injury table. They are always considered to be Out Cold.

Out of Control: During the Wrap-up step of the Post-battle Sequence, if a Chaos Spawn took part in the battle there is a chance they will escape. Their controller nominates up to three Fighters from the gang who did not go Out of Action during the battle; roll a D6 for each Fighter. If at least one Fighter rolls a 4+, the Chaos Spawn is restrained and remains with the gang. otherwise they escape into the depths of the underhive; the Chaos Spawn goes into Recovery while the gang retrieves it. Additionally, if any Fighter rolls a 1, the Chaos Spawn lashes out at them. Roll on the Lasting Injury table for them and apply the result immediately.

Equipment: A Chaos Spawn is armed with tentacles. They may not purchase or be equipped with additional weapons or wargear.

ARMOUR & FIELD ARMOUR

  • Hazard suit10 cr

    10 CREDITS – TP 0

    A fighter wearing a hazard suit is immune to the Blaze (X+) and Rad-phage traits.

  • Mesh armour40 cr

    40 CREDITS – TP 0

    A Fighter equipped with mesh armour increases their Save characteristic by 1 when resolving Hits suffered in close combat.

  • Refractor field50 cr

    50 CREDITS – TP 2

    A refractor field grants its wearer a 5+ Invulnerable save; however, should a natural 1 be rolled when making the Invulnerable save then the refractor field is burned out and cannot be used again for the rest of the battle.

    A refractor field may be combined with other armour and field armour.

PERSONAL EQUIPMENT

  • Cult icon (maximum one per gang)20 cr

    20 credits – Exclusive

    Unlike other items of wargear, a gang may only purchase a single cult icon. This item must be carried by either a Leader or a Champion. When a Fighter that is carrying a cult icon performs the Group Activation action, they may re-roll the Leadership check.

  • Drop rig10 cr

    10 CREDITS – TP 0

    An Active or Suppressed Fighter with a drop rig can perform the Descend action while they are within 1” of the edge of a platform:

    Descend (Single): The Fighter makes a move of up to 3” horizontally and up to 12” vertically. Any vertical movement must be downwards, i.e., towards the ground.

  • Medicae kit20 cr

    20 CREDITS – TP 0

    If a Fighter with a Medicare kit aids another Fighter’s Recovery test, they roll an additional Injury dice and choose which one to keep.

  • Photo-goggles35 cr

    35 CREDITS – TP 0

    A Fighter equipped with photo-goggle increases the value of X in the Visibility (X”) rule by 9” and may see through smoke clouds placed as part of the Smoke trait. Additionally, if a Fighter equipped with photo-goggles is hit by a weapon with the Flash trait, they suffer a -2 modifier to their Initiative check to avoid being blinded.

  • Respirator15 cr

    15 CREDITS – TP 0

    When a Fighter equipped with a respirator is hit by a weapon with the Gas trait, they gain a 5+ Invulnerable save against that weapon.

WEAPON ACCESSORIES

  • Infra-sight10 cr

    10 CREDITS – TP 0

    A weapon fitted with an infra-sight can be fired at targets hidden behind markers created by the Smoke trait. Additionally, the value of X in the Visibility (X”) rule is increased by 9” when using a weapon equipped with an infra-sight.

  • Mono-sight20 cr

    20 CREDITS – TP 0

    When a model performs an Aimed Shot action with a weapon equipped with a mono-sight, they apply a +2 modifier to the Hit roll instead of +1.

MOUNTS

  • Dirt bike35 cr

    35 CREDITS – TP 0

    A Fighter equipped with a dirt bike gains the Mounted Subtype and sets their Movement characteristic to 8”. When they perform a Dash action, they add 5” to their Movement characteristic instead of their Initiative.

CULT ICON

20 credits – Exclusive Unlike other items of wargear, a gang may only purchase a single cult icon. This item must be carried by either a Leader or a Champion. When a Fighter that is carrying a cult icon performs the Group Activation action, they may re-roll the Leadership check.

If the check is failed, the Fighter gains the Insanity condition. 6. Assail (Single) Immediately make a ranged attack against an enemy Fighter within 12” and Line of Sight. If Hit, move the target D3” in any direction and Suppress them. If they come into base contact with another Fighter or any terrain, they stop moving and suffer a Str 3, AP -, L1 Hit. If they come into base contact with another Fighter, that Fighter also suffers a Str 3, AP -, L1 Hit and becomes Suppressed. If the two Fighters belong to different gangs, instead of both becoming Suppressed, they are now Engaged with each other.

CHAOS CORRUPTED GANGS

CHAOS CORRUPTED GANGS SPECIAL RULES

EMBRACING THE CHAOS GODS

During gang creation a player can decide that their gang has been corrupted by the Chaos gods. If they do, they gain the benefits and drawbacks that follow. The following gangs can be Chaos Corrupted: the six clan houses (Cawdor, Delaque, Escher, Orlock and Van Saar) and Palanite Enforcers.

EFFECTS OF CHAOS CORRUPTION

A Chaos Corrupted Gang gains the following benefits and drawbacks:

  • Members of the gang do not benefit from any of the gang’s special rules except for Starting Skills and Skill Access.
  • The gang must select one of the Chaos gods to dedicate themselves to.
  • The gang may perform both the Lead Ritual and Ritual Focus Post-cycle Actions
  • Chaos Helot Cult Witches may be added to the Gang Roster
  • 0-1 Chaos Spawn may be added to the Gang Roster.
  • Leaders and Champions may purchase Chaos Familiars.
  • No Fighters with the Brute, Hanger-on or Pet Subtype may be purchased from the gang’s list.

Dedicated to a Chaos God: When the gang is founded, it must select one of the Chaos gods to dedicate themselves to: the Blood God, the Plague Lord, the Dark Prince or the Architect of Fate.

May Perform Lead Ritual & Ritual Focus Post-cycle Actions: The gang’s Fighters may perform both the Lead Ritual and Ritual Focus Post-cycle Actions. When the gang’s Leader performs the Lead Ritual Post-cycle Action, they can only attempt to invoke the blessing of the Chaos god the gang is dedicated to.

Hiring Chaos Helot Cult Witches & Chaos Spawn: Chaos Corrupted Gangs can include any number of Chaos Helot Cult Witches and up to one Chaos Spawn in their gang. If during the Update Roster step of the Post-cycle Sequence a Chaos Corrupted gang has more than two Chaos Spawn, any excess Chaos Spawn must be removed from the Gang Roster.

Chaos Familiars: Leaders and Champions in Chaos Corrupted Gangs can be equipped with up to one Chaos Familiar each.

No Brutes, Hangers-on or Pets From Core Equipment List: Cutting ties with their original gang, Chaos Corrupted Gangs may not add any Fighters with the Brute or Hanger-on Subtype from their gang list to their Gang Roster, nor may they purchase any Pets from the equipment list.

Erratic Movement: The Movement characteristic for a Chaos Spawn is random; roll each time the Chaos Spawn is activated.

Blessed by the Lord of Skin and Sinew: When a Chaos Spawn is taken Out of Action, do not roll on the Lasting Injury table. They are always considered to be Out Cold.

Out of Control: During the Wrap-up step of the Post-battle Sequence, if a Chaos Spawn took part in the battle there is a chance they will escape. Their controller nominates up to three Fighters from the gang who did not go Out of Action during the battle; roll a D6 for each Fighter. If at least one Fighter rolls a 4+, the Chaos Spawn is restrained and remains with the gang. otherwise they escape into the depths of the underhive; the Chaos Spawn goes into Recovery while the gang retrieves it. Additionally, if any Fighter rolls a 1, the Chaos Spawn lashes out at them. Roll on the Lasting Injury table for them and apply the result immediately.

Equipment: A Chaos Spawn is armed with warped appendages. They may not purchase or be equipped with additional weapons or wargear.

ARMOUR & FIELD ARMOUR

  • Mesh armour40 cr

    40 CREDITS – TP 0

    A Fighter equipped with mesh armour increases their Save characteristic by 1 when resolving Hits suffered in close combat.

  • Refractor field50 cr

    50 CREDITS – TP 2

    A refractor field grants its wearer a 5+ Invulnerable save; however, should a natural 1 be rolled when making the Invulnerable save then the refractor field is burned out and cannot be used again for the rest of the battle.

    A refractor field may be combined with other armour and field armour.

PERSONAL EQUIPMENT

  • Corpse grinder cult icon40 cr

    40 credits – Exclusive

    Only one Fighter in a gang may carry a Corpse Grinder Cult icon; this must be a Fighter with either the Leader or Champion Subtype. A Fighter cannot carry more than one icon. This symbol of blood and gore serves to work members of the cult into a frenzy, throwing themselves at their enemies in a crimson rage. If the Fighter carrying this icon is Active, they may make the following action:

    Enrage (Single): All friendly Fighters that are completely within 6” of this Fighter, that have a Ready marker and are Active, add D3” to their Movement characteristic until the End phase of this round.

  • Drop rig10 cr

    10 CREDITS – TP 0

    An Active or Suppressed Fighter with a drop rig can perform the Descend action while they are within 1” of the edge of a platform:

    Descend (Single): The Fighter makes a move of up to 3” horizontally and up to 12” vertically. Any vertical movement must be downwards, i.e., towards the ground.

  • Medicae kit20 cr

    20 CREDITS – TP 0

    If a Fighter with a Medicare kit aids another Fighter’s Recovery test, they roll an additional Injury dice and choose which one to keep.

  • Photo-goggles35 cr

    35 CREDITS – TP 0

    A Fighter equipped with photo-goggle increases the value of X in the Visibility (X”) rule by 9” and may see through smoke clouds placed as part of the Smoke trait. Additionally, if a Fighter equipped with photo-goggles is hit by a weapon with the Flash trait, they suffer a -2 modifier to their Initiative check to avoid being blinded.

  • Respirator15 cr

    15 CREDITS – TP 0

    When a Fighter equipped with a respirator is hit by a weapon with the Gas trait, they gain a 5+ Invulnerable save against that weapon.

MOUNTS

  • Dirt bike35 cr

    35 CREDITS – TP 0

    A Fighter equipped with a dirt bike gains the Mounted Subtype and sets their Movement characteristic to 8”. When they perform a Dash action, they add 5” to their Movement characteristic instead of their Initiative.

    40 CREDITS – TP 0

    A Fighter equipped with mesh armour increases their Save characteristic by 1 when resolving Hits suffered in close combat.

  • Refractor field50 cr

    50 CREDITS – TP 2

    A refractor field grants its wearer a 5+ Invulnerable save; however, should a natural 1 be rolled when making the Invulnerable save then the refractor field is burned out and cannot be used again for the rest of the battle.

    A refractor field may be combined with other armour and field armour.

PERSONAL EQUIPMENT

  • Bio-booster25 cr

    25 CREDITS – TP 0

    The first time in each battle that the bearer gains the Injured condition, reduce the Lethality characteristic of the weapon damaging them by 1. If the Lethality characteristic is now zero, roll 2 Injury dice instead of 1 and the bearer chooses which to apply; the other dice is discarded.

  • Drop rig10 cr

    10 CREDITS – TP 0

    An Active or Suppressed Fighter with a drop rig can perform the Descend action while they are within 1” of the edge of a platform:

    Descend (Single): The Fighter makes a move of up to 3” horizontally and up to 12” vertically. Any vertical movement must be downwards, i.e., towards the ground.

  • Medicae kit20 cr

    20 CREDITS – TP 0

    If a Fighter with a Medicare kit aids another Fighter’s Recovery test, they roll an additional Injury dice and choose which one to keep.

  • Servo-harness – partial100 cr

    100 CREDITS – TP 2

    A Fighter wearing a partial servo-harness gains a +2 modifier to their Strength characteristic and a +1 modifier to their Toughness characteristic. This may take them above their maximum characteristics but it is not a permanene increase and will be lost should the servo-harness be lost or cease to function for any reason.

    However, a Fighter wearing a partial servo-harness reduces their Movement and Initiative characteristics by 1. This item cannot be combined with a servo-claw or any other type of servo-harness.

  • Stimm-slug stash25 cr

    25 CREDITS – TP 0

    Once per battle, a Fighter equipped with a stimm-slug stash may use it at the start of their activation. Until their next activation increase their Movement, Strength and Toughness characteristics by 2. At the start of their next activation, these effects wear off and the Fighter’s controller must roll a D6; on a 2+ nothing happens, but on a result of 1 they suffer a bad reaction to the stimms – they suffer a Str , AP -, L1 Hit that automatically wounds with no saves allowed.

WEAPON ACCESSORIES

  • Infra-sight10 cr

    10 CREDITS – TP 0

    A weapon fitted with an infra-sight can be fired at targets hidden behind markers created by the Smoke trait. Additionally, the value of X in the Visibility (X”) rule is increased by 9” when using a weapon equipped with an infra-sight.

  • Mono-sight20 cr

    20 CREDITS – TP 0

    When a model performs an Aimed Shot action with a weapon equipped with a mono-sight, they apply a +2 modifier to the Hit roll instead of +1.

  • Telescopic sight20 cr

    20 CREDITS – TP 1

    A weapon fitted with a telescopic sight reduces the benefit a model gains to their Armour save for being in cover by 1 while within the weapon’s Long Range.

GANG SPECIAL RULES

Cult Uprising: Genestealer Cult Fighters apply a +1 modifier to the dice roll when attempting to perform the Coup de Grâce action.

Extra Arm: This option is available to some Fighters in a Genestealer Cult gang and will be stated in the Fighter’s entry. A Fighter with this ability treats the Braced Shot action as a Single action instead of a Double action.

Additionally, the Fighter may carry four weapons rather than the normal three and is always considered to be armed with the clawed arm weapon (which does not take up one of their allowed weapons):

CULT ICON

20 credits – Exclusive Unlike other items of wargear, a gang may only purchase a single cult icon. This item must be carried by either a Leader of Champion. When a Fighter that is carrying a cult icon performs the Group Activation action, they may re-roll the Leadership check.

GENESTEALER CULT WYRD POWERS

Genestealer Cult Adepts and any Genestealer Corrupted gang Leader upgraded to have the Wyrd Subtype have access to the Genestealer Cult Wyrd Powers listed below, and treat these Powers as one of their Primary Skill Sets.

1. Hypnosis (Single) Select an enemy Fighter that is both within 9” and Line of Sight of the Adept, and that has a Ready marker. That Fighter must end their next activation closer to the Adept than they were at the start of their activation. If this is not possible the Fighter suffers a Str -, AP -, L1 Hit that Wounds automatically and ignores all saves.

2. Unbreakable Will (Free), Continuous Effect Whenever a Cool or Willpower check is made for a friendly Fighter within 9” of the Adept, use the Adept’s Cool or Willpower characteristic instead of the Fighter’s (whichever is appropriate).

3. Zealot (Single), Continuous Effect All friendly Fighters within 9” of the Adept gain the Hatred (Everything) Condition.

4. Mind Control (Single) Choose a single enemy Fighter that is both within 9” and Line of Sight of this Fighter. That Fighter immediately makes a Shoot action, even if they have already activated this round, targeting an eligible Fighter from their gang, chosen by this Fighter’s controlling player.

5. Assail (Single) Immediately make a ranged attack against an enemy Fighter within 12” and Line of Sight. If Hit, move the target D3” in any direction and Suppress them. If this movement would cause a Fighter to fall, they stop at the edge of the platform and test to see if they fall. If they come into base contact with another Fighter or any terrain, they stop moving and suffer a Str 3, Ap -, L1 Hit. If they come into base contact with another Fighter, that Fighter also suffers a Str 3, AP, L1 Hit and becomes Suppressed. If the two Fighters belong to different gangs, instead of both of them becoming Suppressed, they are now Engaged with each other.

6. Force Wave (Single) Any enemy Fighters within 3” of the Adept are immediately pushed D3+1” directly away. If this movement would cause a Fighter to fall, they stop at the edge of the platform and test to see if they fall. If they come into base contact with another Fighter or any terrain, they stop moving and suffer a Str 3, Ap -, L1 Hit. If they come into base contact with another Fighter, that Fighter also suffers a Str 3, Ap -, L1 Hit and becomes Suppressed. If the two Fighters belong to different gangs, instead of both of them becoming Suppressed, they are not Engaged with each other.

GENESTEALER CULT CORRUPTED GANGS

GENESTEALER CULT CORRUPTED GANGS SPECIAL RULES

GENESTEALER INFESTATION

During gang creation a player can decide that their gang has been corrupted by a Genestealer Cult. If they do, they gain the benefits and drawbacks that follow. The following gangs can become a Genestealer Cult Corrupted Gang: the six clan houses (Cawdor, Delaque, Escher, Orlock and Van Saar) and Palanite Enforcers.

EFFECTS OF GENESTEALER CULT CORRUPTION

A Genestealer Cult Corrupted Gang gains the following benefits and drawbacks:

  • Members of the gang do not benefit from any of the gang’s special rules except for Starting Skills and Skill Access.
  • The gang Leader may be upgraded to be a Wyrd.
  • 0-2 Genestealer Cult Aberrants may be added to the Gang Roster.
  • 0-2 Genestealer Cult Abominants may be added to the Gang Roster.
  • Leaders and Champions may purchase Psychic Familiars.
  • Prospects maybe given the Extra Arm rule for +20 credits when added to the

Gang Roster.

  • No Fighters with the Brute, Hanger-on or Pet Subtype may be purchased from the gang’s list.

Upgrading the Leader to a Wyrd: The Leader of a Genestealer Cult Corrupted Gang can be upgraded to become a Wyrd for +35 credits. This cost is either paid during the Post-cycle Sequence and requires the Leader to forgo any Post-cycle Actions and to not be In Recovery, or it may be selected when they are added to the Gang Roster. Once the Leader has been upgraded, they gain the Wyrd Subtype and can use a single Wyrd power from the Genestealer Cult Wyrd Powers list. Thereafter, they count new Genestealer Cult Corrupted Gang Wyrd Powers as one of their Primary Skill Sets.

Hiring Genestealer Cult Aberrants & Genestealer Cult Abominants: Genestealer Cult Corrupted Gangs can include up to two Genestealer Cult Aberrants and up to two Genestealer Cult Abominants in their gang.

Psychic Familiars: Leaders and Champions in Genestealer Cult Corrupted Gangs can be equipped with up to one Psychic Familiar each.

Prospects From Earlier Generations: Genestealer Cult Corrupted Gang may give any Prospects the Extra Arm rule for a cost of +20 credits when they are added to the Gang Roster.

No Brutes, Hangers-on or Pets From Core Equipment List: Cutting ties with their original gang, Genestealer Cult Corrupted Gangs may not add any Fighters with the Brute or Hanger-on Subtype from their gang list to their Gang Roster, nor may they purchase any Pets from the equipment list.

GANG SPECIAL RULES

A House Divided: When a Cawdor gang is founded, it must be declared to follow either the Path of the Pious or the Path of the Fanatic. Depending on the choice made, the following rules are in effect:

  • The Path of the Pious

Pious Warriors: The leader of a Cawdor gang that follows the Path of the Pious must have the Pious Subtype. If they die, any Fighter with the Fanatic Subtype is ineligible to replace them. Additionally, a Fanatic Fighter may not be added to a Gang Roster if it would take the number of Fanatic Fighters in a gang above the number of Pious Fighters.

Without Number: When forming starting crews for a battle, at the end of the Choose Crews step of the Pre-battle Sequence, a Cawdor gang following the Path of the Pious may include one additional Prospect in their starting crew.

  • The Path of the Fanatic

Fanatic Warriors: The leader of a Cawdor gang that follows the Path of the Fanatic must have the Fanatic Subtype. If they die, any Fighter with the Pious Subtype is ineligible to replace them. Additionally, a Pious Fighter may not be added to a Gang Roster if it would take the number of Pious Fighters in a gang above the number of Fanatic Fighters.

Fanatical: A Cawdor gang that follows the Path of the Fanatic may re-roll Bottle checks of a natural 11 or 12.

Starting Skills: When added to a Gang Roster, all Cawdor Leaders and Champions may select one skill from one of their Primary Skill Sets.

Skill Access: This gang’s Fighters have access to the following Skill Sets:

ARMOUR & FIELD ARMOUR

  • Mesh armour40 cr

    40 CREDITS – TP 0

    A Fighter equipped with mesh armour increases their Save characteristic by 1 when resolving Hits suffered in close combat.

  • Refractor field50 cr

    50 CREDITS – TP 2

    A refractor field grants its wearer a 5+ Invulnerable save; however, should a natural 1 be rolled when making the Invulnerable save then the refractor field is burned out and cannot be used again for the rest of the battle.

    A refractor field may be combined with other armour and field armour.

PERSONAL EQUIPMENT

  • Bomb delivery rats30 cr

    30 credits – Exclusive

    A Fighter equipped with bomb delivery rats may perform the Prime Bomb Rat action.

    Prime Bomb Rat (Single): Select a grenade with the Blast (3”/5”) trait the Fighter is equipped with that is not Out of Ammo and make an Ammo (X+) test for them as if the grenade had been fired. Then, place a bomb delivery rat in base contact with this Fighter which then immediately activates. At the start of each round, after rolling for Priority but before the first model activates, all bomb delivery rats activate. When a bomb delivery rat activates, follow these instructions:

    • If they are within 9” of the Fighter who placed them, that Fighter’s controlling player may choose which direction they move in, otherwise they move in a direction dictated by the Scatter dice.

    • When they activate they move 6” in a straight line, are not slowed by terrain, have the Clamber skill, can never fall or be pinned, and automatically pass Agility tests to jump gaps of up to 2”.

    • If they come up to a gap larger than 2” or impassable terrain, they will stop.

    • If they move within 1” of any model (other than the Fighter who placed them), they stop and may explode. Roll a D6. On a 2+, the grenade explodes; centre it on the bomb delivery rat. On a roll of a 1, the grenade fails to explode and the bomb delivery rat escapes. Regardless of the result, remove the bomb delivery rat from the battlefield.

    • The bomb delivery rat may be targeted by close combat and ranged attacks. All attempts to hit them suffer a -1 modifier to the Hit roll. If the rat is Hit, roll a D6; on a 4+, the grenade explodes (see above), otherwise the bomb delivery rat escapes.

    Either way, remove them from the battlefield.

ARMOUR & FIELD ARMOUR

  • Mesh armour40 cr

    40 CREDITS – TP 0

    A Fighter equipped with mesh armour increases their Save characteristic by 1 when resolving Hits suffered in close combat.

  • Refractor field50 cr

    50 CREDITS – TP 2

    A refractor field grants its wearer a 5+ Invulnerable save; however, should a natural 1 be rolled when making the Invulnerable save then the refractor field is burned out and cannot be used again for the rest of the battle.

    A refractor field may be combined with other armour and field armour.

PERSONAL EQUIPMENT

  • Book of the Redemption50 cr

    50 credits – Exclusive

    A Fighter equipped with a Book of the Redemption may perform the Words of Wrath action:

    Words of Wrath (Single): This Fighter read aloud from the Book of the Redemption. Until the End phase of this round, any friendly Fanatic Fighters that are within 6” of this Fighter when their activation starts may either re-roll the D6 when performing a Charge action, or may re-roll a single roll of a natural 1 when making a Hit roll.

  • Drop rig10 cr

    10 CREDITS – TP 0

    An Active or Suppressed Fighter with a drop rig can perform the Descend action while they are within 1” of the edge of a platform:

    Descend (Single): The Fighter makes a move of up to 3” horizontally and up to 12” vertically. Any vertical movement must be downwards, i.e., towards the ground.

  • Medicae kit20 cr

    20 CREDITS – TP 0

    If a Fighter with a Medicare kit aids another Fighter’s Recovery test, they roll an additional Injury dice and choose which one to keep.

  • Photo-goggles35 cr

    35 CREDITS – TP 0

    A Fighter equipped with photo-goggle increases the value of X in the Visibility (X”) rule by 9” and may see through smoke clouds placed as part of the Smoke trait. Additionally, if a Fighter equipped with photo-goggles is hit by a weapon with the Flash trait, they suffer a -2 modifier to their Initiative check to avoid being blinded.

  • Pyromantic mantle30 cr

    30 credits – Exclusive

    Any attacks made with close combat weapons carried by a Fighter with a pyromantic mantle gain the Blaze (5+) trait during that Fighter’s activation (note: if the weapon already has the Blaze (X) trait then this wargear has no effect.

  • Respirator15 cr

    15 CREDITS – TP 0

    When a Fighter equipped with a respirator is hit by a weapon with the Gas trait, they gain a 5+ Invulnerable save against that weapon.

WEAPON ACCESSORIES

  • Infra-sight10 cr

    10 CREDITS – TP 0

    A weapon fitted with an infra-sight can be fired at targets hidden behind markers created by the Smoke trait. Additionally, the value of X in the Visibility (X”) rule is increased by 9” when using a weapon equipped with an infra-sight.

  • Mono-sight20 cr

    20 CREDITS – TP 0

    When a model performs an Aimed Shot action with a weapon equipped with a mono-sight, they apply a +2 modifier to the Hit roll instead of +1.

MOUNTS

  • Dirt bike35 cr

    35 CREDITS – TP 0

    A Fighter equipped with a dirt bike gains the Mounted Subtype and sets their Movement characteristic to 8”. When they perform a Dash action, they add 5” to their Movement characteristic instead of their Initiative.

  • Ridge Walker45 cr

    Exclusive

    A Fighter equipped with a Ridge Walker gains the Mounted and Agile Subtypes, applies a +1 modifier to any Agility test they make and sets their Movement characteristic to 8”. When they perform a Dash action, they add 5” to their Movement characteristic instead of their Initiative.

PERSONAL EQUIPMENT

BOMB DELIVERY RATS

30 credits – Exclusive A Fighter equipped with bomb delivery rats may perform the Prime Bomb Rat action.

Prime Bomb Rat (Single): Select a grenade with the Blast (3”/5”) trait the Fighter is equipped with that is not Out of Ammo and make an Ammo (X+) test for them as if the grenade had been fired. Then, place a bomb delivery rat in base contact with this Fighter which then immediately activates. At the start of each round, after rolling for Priority but before the first model activates, all bomb delivery rats activate. When a bomb delivery rat activates, follow these instructions:

  • If they are within 9” of the Fighter who placed them, that Fighter’s controlling player may choose which direction they move in, otherwise they move in a direction dictated by the Scatter dice.
  • When they activate they move 6” in a straight line, are not slowed by terrain, have the Clamber skill, can never fall or be pinned, and automatically pass Agility tests to jump gaps of up to 2”.
  • If they come up to a gap larger than 2” or impassable terrain, they will stop.
  • If they move within 1” of any model (other than the Fighter who placed them), they stop and may explode. Roll a D6. On a 2+, the grenade explodes; centre it on the bomb delivery rat. On a roll of a 1, the grenade fails to explode and the bomb delivery rat escapes. Regardless of the result, remove the bomb delivery rat from the battlefield.
  • The bomb delivery rat may be targeted by close combat and ranged attacks. All attempts to hit them suffer a -1 modifier to the Hit roll. If the rat is Hit, roll a D6; on a 4+, the grenade explodes (see above), otherwise the bomb delivery rat escapes.

Either way, remove them from the battlefield.

BOOK OF THE REDEMPTION

50 credits – Exclusive A Fighter equipped with a Book of the Redemption may perform the Words of Wrath action:

Words of Wrath (Single): This Fighter read aloud from the Book of the Redemption. Until the End phase of this round, any friendly Fanatic Fighters that are within 6” of this Fighter when their activation starts may either re-roll the D6 when performing a Charge action, or may re-roll a single roll of a natural 1 when making a Hit roll.

CULT ICON

40 credits – Exclusive Unlike other items of wargear, a gang may only purchase a single cult icon. This item must be carried by either a Leader or a Champion. When a Fighter that is carrying a cult icon performs the Group Activation action, they may re-roll the Leadership check.

PYROMANTIC MANTLE

30 credits – Exclusive Any attacks made with close combat weapons carried by a Fighter with a pyromantic mantle gain the Blaze (5+) trait during that Fighter’s activation (note: if the weapon already has the Blaze (X) trait then this wargear has no effect.

MOUNTS

RIDGE WALKER

Exclusive A Fighter equipped with a Ridge Walker gains the Mounted and Agile Subtypes, applies a +1 modifier to any Agility test they make and sets their Movement characteristic to 8”. When they perform a Dash action, they add 5” to their Movement characteristic instead of their Initiative.

Leash Range: A Psychoteric Wyrm has a 12” Leash range.

Psychoteric Node: When a Delaque Wyrd uses a Psychoteric Power, they may nominate an Active Psychoteric Wyrm they own that is within Leash range through which to channel that Power. The effect of the Psychoteric Power is worked out from the model representing the Psychoteric Wyrm, rather than from the model representing the Fighter. In other words, Line of Sight, distance, range and so forth are all measured from the Psychoteric Wyrm, not from the Fighter.

Burrowing: A Psychoteric Wyrm is able to burrow beneath and through the metal and rockcrete floors of the underhive, passing quickly through hidden crawl spaces and buried vents, before emerging elsewhere. A Psychoteric Wyrm may move freely under impassable terrain if it has sufficient movement to do so, but may not end its movement on or within impassable terrain.

Equipment: A Psychoteric Wyrm is armed with ferocious jaws. They may not purchase or be equipped with additional weapons or wargear.

PSYCHOMANCER’S HARNESS

35 credits – Exclusive A Fighter wearing a psychomancer’s harness increases their Movement characteristic by 2”; this may take the Fighter’s Movement characteristic above the maximum.

Additionally, when this Fighter climbs, the vertical distance they move is not halved. In other words, they always count as climbing up or down a ladder. A Fighter may not be equipped with both a psychomancer’s harness and a servo-harness.

PSYCHOTERIC WHISPERS

The following are Wyrd Powers are available to Delaque Fighters. Any Delaque Fighter with the Wyrd Subtype may select Psychoteric Whispers as an Advancement as if they were a Primary Skill Set.

1. Terrible Truths (Single): Choose a single enemy Fighter that is within 6” and Line of Sight of the Wyrd. That Fighter must make a Willpower check. If this check is failed, they gain the Insanity Condition.

2. Psychoteric Lure (Single): Choose a single enemy Fighter that currently has a Ready marker and is within 6” and Line of Sight of the Wyrd. The opposing player must activate that Fighter next. The chosen Fighter cannot perform the Group Activation action when next activated.

3. Deceiful Thoughts (Double): Choose a single enemy Fighter that is within 6” and Line of Sight of the Wyrd. That Fighter immediately makes a Willpower check. If this check is failed, the Wyrd’s controlling player may immediately move that Fighter up to their Movement characteristic in any direction (note: this move may not be used to move enemy Fighters off ledges, into dangerous terrain or any other part of the battlefield harmful to them).

4. Cacophony of Silence (Single), Continuous Effect: While this power is maintained, all enemy Fighters within 6” and Line of Sight of the Wyrd must re- roll successful Hit rolls when making a ranged attack.

5. A Perfect Void (Free), Continuous Effect: While this power is maintained, the Wyrd counts as always being in cover and within a weapon’s Long Range to all enemy Fighters within 10”.

6. Eternal Slumber (Single): Choose a Seriously Injured enemy Fighter within 3” and Line of Sight of the Wyrd, they immediately go Out of Action.

ARMOUR & FIELD ARMOUR

  • Mesh armour40 cr

    40 CREDITS – TP 0

    A Fighter equipped with mesh armour increases their Save characteristic by 1 when resolving Hits suffered in close combat.

  • Refractor field50 cr

    50 CREDITS – TP 2

    A refractor field grants its wearer a 5+ Invulnerable save; however, should a natural 1 be rolled when making the Invulnerable save then the refractor field is burned out and cannot be used again for the rest of the battle.

    A refractor field may be combined with other armour and field armour.

PERSONAL EQUIPMENT

  • Drop rig10 cr

    10 CREDITS – TP 0

    An Active or Suppressed Fighter with a drop rig can perform the Descend action while they are within 1” of the edge of a platform:

    Descend (Single): The Fighter makes a move of up to 3” horizontally and up to 12” vertically. Any vertical movement must be downwards, i.e., towards the ground.

  • Medicae kit20 cr

    20 CREDITS – TP 0

    If a Fighter with a Medicare kit aids another Fighter’s Recovery test, they roll an additional Injury dice and choose which one to keep.

  • Photo-goggles35 cr

    35 CREDITS – TP 0

    A Fighter equipped with photo-goggle increases the value of X in the Visibility (X”) rule by 9” and may see through smoke clouds placed as part of the Smoke trait. Additionally, if a Fighter equipped with photo-goggles is hit by a weapon with the Flash trait, they suffer a -2 modifier to their Initiative check to avoid being blinded.

  • Respirator15 cr

    15 CREDITS – TP 0

    When a Fighter equipped with a respirator is hit by a weapon with the Gas trait, they gain a 5+ Invulnerable save against that weapon.

WEAPON ACCESSORIES

  • Las-projector20 cr

    20 CREDITS – TP 1

    A weapon fitted with a las-projector reduces the benefit a model gains to their Armour save for being in cover by 1 while within the weapon’s Short Range.

MOUNTS

  • Dirt bike35 cr

ARMOUR & FIELD ARMOUR

  • Mesh armour40 cr

    40 CREDITS – TP 0

    A Fighter equipped with mesh armour increases their Save characteristic by 1 when resolving Hits suffered in close combat.

  • Refractor field50 cr

    50 CREDITS – TP 2

    A refractor field grants its wearer a 5+ Invulnerable save; however, should a natural 1 be rolled when making the Invulnerable save then the refractor field is burned out and cannot be used again for the rest of the battle.

    A refractor field may be combined with other armour and field armour.

PERSONAL EQUIPMENT

  • Drop rig10 cr

    10 CREDITS – TP 0

    An Active or Suppressed Fighter with a drop rig can perform the Descend action while they are within 1” of the edge of a platform:

    Descend (Single): The Fighter makes a move of up to 3” horizontally and up to 12” vertically. Any vertical movement must be downwards, i.e., towards the ground.

  • Medicae kit20 cr

    20 CREDITS – TP 0

    If a Fighter with a Medicare kit aids another Fighter’s Recovery test, they roll an additional Injury dice and choose which one to keep.

  • Photo-goggles35 cr

    35 CREDITS – TP 0

    A Fighter equipped with photo-goggle increases the value of X in the Visibility (X”) rule by 9” and may see through smoke clouds placed as part of the Smoke trait. Additionally, if a Fighter equipped with photo-goggles is hit by a weapon with the Flash trait, they suffer a -2 modifier to their Initiative check to avoid being blinded.

  • Respirator15 cr

    15 CREDITS – TP 0

    When a Fighter equipped with a respirator is hit by a weapon with the Gas trait, they gain a 5+ Invulnerable save against that weapon.

  • Stimm-slug stash25 cr

    25 CREDITS – TP 0

    Once per battle, a Fighter equipped with a stimm-slug stash may use it at the start of their activation. Until their next activation increase their Movement, Strength and Toughness characteristics by 2. At the start of their next activation, these effects wear off and the Fighter’s controller must roll a D6; on a 2+ nothing happens, but on a result of 1 they suffer a bad reaction to the stimms – they suffer a Str , AP -, L1 Hit that automatically wounds with no saves allowed.

WEAPON ACCESSORIES

  • Telescopic sight20 cr

    20 CREDITS – TP 1

    A weapon fitted with a telescopic sight reduces the benefit a model gains to their Armour save for being in cover by 1 while within the weapon’s Long Range.

MOUNTS

  • Dirt bike35 cr

    35 CREDITS – TP 0

    A Fighter equipped with a dirt bike gains the Mounted Subtype and sets their Movement characteristic to 8”. When they perform a Dash action, they add 5” to their Movement characteristic instead of their Initiative.

  • Goliath Mauler100 cr

    Exclusive

    A Fighter equipped with a Goliath Mauler gains the Mounted Subtype and sets their Movement characteristic to 7”. When they perform a Dash action, they add 4” to their Movement characteristic instead of their Initiative.

ARMOUR & FIELD ARMOUR

  • Mesh armour40 cr

    40 CREDITS – TP 0

    A Fighter equipped with mesh armour increases their Save characteristic by 1 when resolving Hits suffered in close combat.

  • Refractor field50 cr

    50 CREDITS – TP 2

    A refractor field grants its wearer a 5+ Invulnerable save; however, should a natural 1 be rolled when making the Invulnerable save then the refractor field is burned out and cannot be used again for the rest of the battle.

    A refractor field may be combined with other armour and field armour.

PERSONAL EQUIPMENT

  • Bio-booster25 cr

    25 CREDITS – TP 0

    The first time in each battle that the bearer gains the Injured condition, reduce the Lethality characteristic of the weapon damaging them by 1. If the Lethality characteristic is now zero, roll 2 Injury dice instead of 1 and the bearer chooses which to apply; the other dice is discarded.

  • Drop rig10 cr

    10 CREDITS – TP 0

    An Active or Suppressed Fighter with a drop rig can perform the Descend action while they are within 1” of the edge of a platform:

    Descend (Single): The Fighter makes a move of up to 3” horizontally and up to 12” vertically. Any vertical movement must be downwards, i.e., towards the ground.

  • Medicae kit20 cr

    20 CREDITS – TP 0

    If a Fighter with a Medicare kit aids another Fighter’s Recovery test, they roll an additional Injury dice and choose which one to keep.

  • Photo-goggles35 cr

    35 CREDITS – TP 0

    A Fighter equipped with photo-goggle increases the value of X in the Visibility (X”) rule by 9” and may see through smoke clouds placed as part of the Smoke trait. Additionally, if a Fighter equipped with photo-goggles is hit by a weapon with the Flash trait, they suffer a -2 modifier to their Initiative check to avoid being blinded.

  • Respirator15 cr

    15 CREDITS – TP 0

    When a Fighter equipped with a respirator is hit by a weapon with the Gas trait, they gain a 5+ Invulnerable save against that weapon.

  • Servo-harness – partial100 cr

    100 CREDITS – TP 2

    A Fighter wearing a partial servo-harness gains a +2 modifier to their Strength characteristic and a +1 modifier to their Toughness characteristic. This may take them above their maximum characteristics but it is not a permanene increase and will be lost should the servo-harness be lost or cease to function for any reason.

    However, a Fighter wearing a partial servo-harness reduces their Movement and Initiative characteristics by 1. This item cannot be combined with a servo-claw or any other type of servo-harness.

  • Servo-harness – full130 cr

    130 CREDITS – TP 3

    A Fighter wearing a full servo-harness gains all of the benefits of a partial servo- harness, but without the negative modifiers to their Movement and Initiative charcteristics. This item cannot be combined with a servo-claw or any other type of servo-harness.

PERSONAL EQUIPMENT

JUMP BOOSTER

Exclusive At the start of their activation, a Fighter equipped with a jump booster may choose to activate it. When a jump booster is activated, for the duration of their activation the Fighter increases their Movement characteristic by 3” and gains the Flying Subtype.

Should a Fighter use a jump booster when making a Charge action, for the duration of this activation they may apply both a +1 modifier to each Hit roll they make and a +1 modifier to their Strength characteristic.

Hazardous Equipment: Using a jump booster is not without its risks, and this is never more true than when the user is attempting to use flame weapons or lob grenades. To represent this added danger, during any activation in which a Fighter equipped with a jump booster activates it, any grenades or weapons with the Template trait will also gain the Unstable trait. Once the Fighter’s activation ends, this rule ceases to apply.

ARMOUR & FIELD ARMOUR

  • Light carapace armour (Gunner specialist only)100 cr

    LIGHT: 100 CREDITS – TP 1

    HEAVY: 140 CREDITS – TP 3

    Light: Light carapace armour improves a Fighter’s Save characteristic by 1. In addition, they reduce their Initiative characteristic by 1.

    Heavy: Heavy carapace armour improve’s a Fighter’s Save characteristic by 2. In addition, they reduce their Initiative characteristic by 2 and apply a -1 modifier to all Agility tests they make.

  • Mesh armour40 cr

    40 CREDITS – TP 0

    A Fighter equipped with mesh armour increases their Save characteristic by 1 when resolving Hits suffered in close combat.

  • Refractor field50 cr

    50 CREDITS – TP 2

    A refractor field grants its wearer a 5+ Invulnerable save; however, should a natural 1 be rolled when making the Invulnerable save then the refractor field is burned out and cannot be used again for the rest of the battle.

    A refractor field may be combined with other armour and field armour.

PERSONAL EQUIPMENT

  • Augurspex (Tech specialist only)30 cr

    30 credits – Exclusive

    Enemy Fighters may not be set up within 12” of a Fighter with an augurspex as either Reinforcements or using the Infiltrate skill.

  • Bio-booster25 cr

    25 CREDITS – TP 0

    The first time in each battle that the bearer gains the Injured condition, reduce the Lethality characteristic of the weapon damaging them by 1. If the Lethality characteristic is now zero, roll 2 Injury dice instead of 1 and the bearer chooses which to apply; the other dice is discarded.

  • Drop rig10 cr

    10 CREDITS – TP 0

    An Active or Suppressed Fighter with a drop rig can perform the Descend action while they are within 1” of the edge of a platform:

    Descend (Single): The Fighter makes a move of up to 3” horizontally and up to 12” vertically. Any vertical movement must be downwards, i.e., towards the ground.

  • Grav chute30 cr

    30 CREDITS – TP 0

    If a Fighter with a grav chute falls or jumps down, they never suffer any damage and are never Suppressed.

  • Medicae kit20 cr

    20 CREDITS – TP 0

    If a Fighter with a Medicare kit aids another Fighter’s Recovery test, they roll an additional Injury dice and choose which one to keep.

  • Photo-goggles35 cr

    35 CREDITS – TP 0

    A Fighter equipped with photo-goggle increases the value of X in the Visibility (X”) rule by 9” and may see through smoke clouds placed as part of the Smoke trait. Additionally, if a Fighter equipped with photo-goggles is hit by a weapon with the Flash trait, they suffer a -2 modifier to their Initiative check to avoid being blinded.

  • Refraction cloak (Sniper specialist only)40 cr

    40 credits – Exclusive

    When making a ranged attack against a Fighter equipped with a refraction cloak, the Hit roll suffers a -1 penalty to Hit. This is increased to -2 if the Fighter did not move in their previous activation.

  • Respirator15 cr

    15 CREDITS – TP 0

    When a Fighter equipped with a respirator is hit by a weapon with the Gas trait, they gain a 5+ Invulnerable save against that weapon.

  • Servo-medicae (Medic specialist only)30 cr

    30 credits – Exclusive

    An Active Fighter equipped with a servo-medicae may perform the Auto- medicate action:

    Auto-medicate (Free): When a Fighter performs this action, target either them or a friendly Active or Suppressed Fighter within 3” and make an Intelligence check for this Fighter. If the check is passed then the targeted Fighter regains 1 Wound lost earlier in the battle.

  • Vox array (Tech specialist only)15 cr

    15 credits – Exclusive

    An Active Fighter equipped with a vox array may perform the Group Activation action as a Free action.

WEAPON ACCESSORIES

  • Infra-sight10 cr

    10 CREDITS – TP 0

    A weapon fitted with an infra-sight can be fired at targets hidden behind markers created by the Smoke trait. Additionally, the value of X in the Visibility (X”) rule is increased by 9” when using a weapon equipped with an infra-sight.

  • Las-projector20 cr

    20 CREDITS – TP 1

    A weapon fitted with a las-projector reduces the benefit a model gains to their Armour save for being in cover by 1 while within the weapon’s Short Range.

  • Mono-sight20 cr

    20 CREDITS – TP 0

    When a model performs an Aimed Shot action with a weapon equipped with a mono-sight, they apply a +2 modifier to the Hit roll instead of +1.

  • Telescopic sight20 cr

    20 CREDITS – TP 1

    A weapon fitted with a telescopic sight reduces the benefit a model gains to their Armour save for being in cover by 1 while within the weapon’s Long Range.

ARMOUR & FIELD ARMOUR

  • Carapace armour (light)100 cr

    LIGHT: 100 CREDITS – TP 1

    HEAVY: 140 CREDITS – TP 3

    Light: Light carapace armour improves a Fighter’s Save characteristic by 1. In addition, they reduce their Initiative characteristic by 1.

    Heavy: Heavy carapace armour improve’s a Fighter’s Save characteristic by 2. In addition, they reduce their Initiative characteristic by 2 and apply a -1 modifier to all Agility tests they make.

  • Mesh armour40 cr

    40 CREDITS – TP 0

    A Fighter equipped with mesh armour increases their Save characteristic by 1 when resolving Hits suffered in close combat.

  • Refractor field50 cr

    50 CREDITS – TP 2

    A refractor field grants its wearer a 5+ Invulnerable save; however, should a natural 1 be rolled when making the Invulnerable save then the refractor field is burned out and cannot be used again for the rest of the battle.

    A refractor field may be combined with other armour and field armour.

PERSONAL EQUIPMENT

  • Bio-booster25 cr

    25 CREDITS – TP 0

    The first time in each battle that the bearer gains the Injured condition, reduce the Lethality characteristic of the weapon damaging them by 1. If the Lethality characteristic is now zero, roll 2 Injury dice instead of 1 and the bearer chooses which to apply; the other dice is discarded.

  • Drop rig10 cr

    10 CREDITS – TP 0

    An Active or Suppressed Fighter with a drop rig can perform the Descend action while they are within 1” of the edge of a platform:

    Descend (Single): The Fighter makes a move of up to 3” horizontally and up to 12” vertically. Any vertical movement must be downwards, i.e., towards the ground.

  • Grav chute30 cr

    30 CREDITS – TP 0

    If a Fighter with a grav chute falls or jumps down, they never suffer any damage and are never Suppressed.

  • Medicae kit20 cr

    20 CREDITS – TP 0

    If a Fighter with a Medicare kit aids another Fighter’s Recovery test, they roll an additional Injury dice and choose which one to keep.

  • Photo-goggles35 cr

    35 CREDITS – TP 0

    A Fighter equipped with photo-goggle increases the value of X in the Visibility (X”) rule by 9” and may see through smoke clouds placed as part of the Smoke trait. Additionally, if a Fighter equipped with photo-goggles is hit by a weapon with the Flash trait, they suffer a -2 modifier to their Initiative check to avoid being blinded.

  • Photo-lumens15 cr

    15 CREDITS – TP 0

    Increase the value of X in the Visibility (X”) rule by 9” for this Fighter. This Fighter can always be targeted, regardless of the Visibility (X”) rule.

  • Respirator15 cr

    15 CREDITS – TP 0

    When a Fighter equipped with a respirator is hit by a weapon with the Gas trait, they gain a 5+ Invulnerable save against that weapon.

WEAPON ACCESSORIES

  • Infra-sight10 cr

    10 CREDITS – TP 0

    A weapon fitted with an infra-sight can be fired at targets hidden behind markers created by the Smoke trait. Additionally, the value of X in the Visibility (X”) rule is increased by 9” when using a weapon equipped with an infra-sight.

  • Mono-sight20 cr

    20 CREDITS – TP 0

    When a model performs an Aimed Shot action with a weapon equipped with a mono-sight, they apply a +2 modifier to the Hit roll instead of +1.

MOUNTS

  • Dirt bike35 cr

    35 CREDITS – TP 0

    A Fighter equipped with a dirt bike gains the Mounted Subtype and sets their Movement characteristic to 8”. When they perform a Dash action, they add 5” to their Movement characteristic instead of their Initiative.

  • Svenotar Scout Trike80 cr

SVENOTAR SCOUT TRIKE

80 credits – Exclusive A Fighter equipped with a Svenotar Scout Trike gains the Mounted Subtype amd sets their Movement characteristic to 8”. When they perform a Dash action, they add 5” to their Movement characteristic instead of their Initiative.

A Svenotar Scout Trike is equipped with a Svenotar autogun and may take either of the following options when added to the gang or during any Post-cycle Sequence.

  • Replace the Svenotar autogun with a Svenotar meltagun+70 cr

• During the course of a campaign, they may be given additional Pets purchased from the Malstrain Equipment List.

MALSTRAIN WYRD POWERS

Malstrain Coalescenses and any Malstrain Corrupted gang Leader upgraded to have the Wyrd Sybtype have access to the Malstrain Wyrd Powers listed below, and treat these powers as one of their Primary Skill Sets.

1. Catalyst (Free), Continuous Effect Whenever a friendly Fighter within 12” if this model is taken Out of Action, they may perform a Shoot or Fight action as a Free action before being removed from the battlefield, even if they do not have a Ready marker.

2. Hypnotic Gaze (Double) An enemy Fighter within 9” and Line of Sight of the Wyrd must make an Agility test. If the test if failed, they lose their Ready marker.

3. The Horror (Single) Target an enemy Fighter within 12” – the targeted Fighter must immediately make a Nerve check.

4. Leech Essence (Single) Target an enemy Fighter within 12” and Line of Sight – they suffer a Str 3, Ap -1, L1 Hit. If they take any damage as a result of this attack, the Wyrd may regain a Wound lost earlier in the battle.

5. Paroxysm (Single), Continuous Effect Target an enemy Fighter within 9” and Line of Sight of the Wyrd; while this power is maintained they set their BS and WS to 6+.

6. Aura of Despair (Free), Continuous Effect While this power is maintained, all enemy models within 12” reduce their Cool characteristic by 1.

MALSTRAIN CORRUPTED GANGS

MALSTRAIN CORRUPTED SPECIAL RULES

WILL OF THE PATRIARCH

During gang creation, a player can decide that their gang has been corrupted by the Malstrain taint. If they do, they gain the benefits and drawbacks that follow. The following gangs can be Malstrain corrupted: the six Clan Houses (Cawdor, Delaque, Escher, Goliath, Orlock and Van Saar) and Palanite Enforcers.

EFFECTS OF MALSTRAIN CORRUPTION

A Malstrain corrupted gang gains the following benefits and drawbacks:

  • Members of the gang do not benefit from any of the gang’s special rules except for starting skills and skill access.
  • The gang leader may be upgraded to be a Wyrd.
  • 0-3 Malstrain Genestealers and 0-1 Malstrain Coalescence may be added to the

Gang Roster.

  • Leaders and Champions may purchase Malstrain Tyramites.
  • Any number of Malstrain Brood Scum may be added to the Gang Roster.
  • No Fighters with the Brute, Hanger-on or Pet Subtype may be purchased from the gang’s list.

Upgrading the Leader to a Wyrd: the Leader of a Malstrain corrupted gang can be upgraded to become a Wyrd for +35 credits. This cost is either paid during the Post- cycle Sequence and requires the Leader to forgo any Post-cycle Actions and to not be In Recovery, or it may be selected when they are recruited. Once the Leader has been upgraded, they gain the Wyrd Subtype and can choose one Wyrd power from the Malstrain Wyrd Powers list. Thereafter, they count Malstrain Wyrd Powers as one of their Primary Skill Sets.

Hiring Malstrain Genestealers & Malstrain Coalescence: Malstrain corrupted gangs can include up to three Malstrain Genestealers and up to one Malstrain Coalescence in their gang.

Malstrain Tyramites: Leaders and Champions in Malstrain corrupted gangs can be equipped with up to two Malstrain Tyramites each.

Hiring Malstrain Brood Scum: Malstrain corrupted gangs may add Malstrain Brood Scum to their gang roster as if they were part of their gang list.

No Brutes, Hangers-on or Pets From Core Equipment List: Cutting ties with their original gang, Malstrain corrupted gangs may not add Fighters with the Brute or Hanger-on Subtypes from their gang list to their Gang Roster, nor may they purchase any pets from their equipment list.

GANG SPECIAL RULES

Cult of Personality: All Outcast Fighters within 6” of the gang’s Leader automatically pass any Nerve checks they need to make and are unaffected by models with the Fearsome Condition.

Lead the Masses: There must always be at least three Outcast Hive Scum on the Gang Roster for each Outcast Champion in an Outcast gang. If, during the Update Roster step of the Post-cycle Sequence there are not at least three Outcast Hive Scum for each Outcast Champion, Outcast Champions must be removed from the Gang Roster until this is no longer the case.

Starting Skills: When added to a Gang Roster, all Outcast Leaders and Champions may select one skill from one of their Primary Skill Sets.

Skill Access: This gang’s Fighters have access to the following Skill Sets as determined by their Archetypes.

DESIGNER'S NOTE: ELEVATING A FIGHTER TO LEADER STATUS

There are many kinds of Outcast Leaders that can be created using the profiles, Archetypes and Affiliations presented in this section. It might be, however, that you want to create an Outcast gang centred around an existing fighter from another gang list or Necromunda publication. This is entirely appropriate, as any Fighter might rise up to lead a gang at some point or another in their careers.

  • The first step is to choose a Fighter to become your Outcast Leader. This can be any Fighter with a profile, whether they could normally be part of a gang or not.

Dramatis Personae, Hangers-on and Hired Guns are particularly suited to becoming gang Leaders and should prove easy to convert. Other kinds of Fighters might need more work, and some should probably only be allowed with the agreement of the campaign Arbitrator (as fun as it would be to have a gang of Outcasts led by an intelligent Sumpkroc).

  • The Fighter retains any skills, equipment or special rules they might have. Alternatively, you can replace their skills and equipment with those available to an

Outcast Leader. Whichever option is taken, you need to choose an appropriate Affiliation and Archetype for this Fighter.

  • The Fighter retains their cost in credits, and throughout a campaign gains Experience and can be equipped with wargear like a normal Fighter.
  • The Fighter gains all the special rules an Outcast Leader has.

Note that, due to the incredibly wide variety of Fighters available to be elevated to an Outcast Leader, the campaign Arbitrator always has the final say on whether these rules can be used and how they are applied.

ARCHETYPE

Every Outcast Leader has different strengths and weaknesses. Some are brutal overlords who rule through physical strength, crushing all in their path; others are more cunning, manipulating those around them to do their bidding; others still call upon the powers of the Warp to keep their gang in line. Archetypes allow you to further customize your Outcast Leader by giving them access to different Skill Sets.

There are five different Archetypes: Brawler, Gunslinger, Mastermind, Survivor, and Wyrd. When an Outcast Leader is recruited for an Outcast gang they must choose one of these Archetypes, and it may not be changed later on. This Archetype will also determine the skills available to all Outcast models except Champions (note:

Champions may choose a different Archetype to their gang's Leader).

AFFILIATION

To represent the huge variety of potential Outcast Leaders, when an Outcast gang is created its Leader must choose an Affiliation. An Affiliation is a glimpse into the origins of the Leader, or speaks to the contacts they still maintain with those more mainstream members of hive society. There are four different Affiliations an Outcast Leader can choose from: Clanless, Clan House, Aranthian or Mutant. Each comes with its own advantages and disadvantages, but most importantly will determine the equipment that the Outcast Leader and their gang has access to. Once the choice of Affiliation has been made, it cannot be changed – not even an Outcast can escape their past.

CLANLESS OUTCAST GANGS

A Clanless Outcast Leader and their gang gain the following benefits:

  • Clanless Outcast gangs gain additional TPs as covered below:
  • At gang creation, each Leader and Champion in a Clanless Outcast gang gains an additional 1 TP that may be spent on weapons and wargear from the Trading Post.
  • During each Post-cycle Sequence, the first Visit Trading Post Post-cycle Action performed by a Clanless Outcast gang generates an additional 1 TP.

CLAN HOUSE OUTCAST GANGS

A Clan House Outcast Leader and their gang gain the following benefits:

  • When a Clan House Outcast gang is created, you must choose one of the six Clan

Houses for them to affiliate with: Cawdor, Delaque, Escher, Goliath, Van Saar or Orlock. For scenario or campaign purposes, the Outcast gang is considered to be a Clan House gang of the chosen type.

  • Leaders and Champions in a Clan House Outcast gang may purchase weapons and wargear normally restricted to their house equipment lists, including Pets, at gang creation and during each Post-cycle Sequence.

MUTANT OUTCAST GANGS

A Mutant Outcast Leader and their gang gain the following benefits:

  • When a Fighter is added to a Mutant Outcast gang’s Gang Roster they may purchase a number of Mutations, depending on their Subtype, from the list.
  • Leaders and Champions may purchase up to two Mutations.
  • Gangers may purchase only one Mutation.

ARANTHIAN OUTCAST GANGS

An Aranthian Outcast Leader and their gang gain the following benefits:

  • Leaders and Champions in an Aranthian Outcast gang may purchase items from the Aranthian equipment list at gang creation and during each Post-cycle

Sequence.

MUTATIONS

When added to a Mutant Outcast gang’s Gang Roster, Fighters may purchase Mutations from the following list:

VOID SOUL

15 credits The mutant cannot be targeted by Wyrd Powers – though indirect damage from Wyrd Powers, such as telekinetically-thrown objects or weapons acquired by the use of Wyrd Powers, can still hurt them.

EXTRA APPENDAGE

20 credits The Mutant increases their Attacks characteristic by 1. In addition, they may be equipped with four weapons rather than three.

HORRIFIC APPEARANCE

15 credits The Mutant is subject to the Fearsome Condition.

MASSIVE CLAWS

35 credits The Mutant is equipped with the following weapon, which does not count as one of their allowed weapons:

WeaponSRLRStrAPLTraits
Massive clawsE-S+1-11Breaching (6+)Если атака ранит и бросок на ранение не меньше X, спасброски брони делать нельзя., MeleeОружие для атак, пока модель Engaged.

NEEDLE SPINES

15 credits A Mutant with this Mutation may not wear any armour or field armour unless it may be combined with other armours. The Mutant increases their Save characteristic by 1 when resolving Hits suffered in close combat. In addition, once per battle, the Mutant may perform the Fire Spines action:

Fire Spines (Single): All other models (friend and foe), within 3” of the Mutant suffer a Str -, AP -, L1 Hit with the Toxin (3+) trait. After this action has been performed, the Mutant gains no further bonus to their Save characteristic from this Mutation for the remainder of the battle.

TENTACLES

10 credits The Mutant may re-roll failed Agility tests.

TOXIC BLOOD

15 credits When this mutant suffers an unsaved Wound, immediately make an Agility test for all other Fighters (friend or foe) within 1" of the Mutant. Those that fail the test suffer a Str -, AP -, L1 Hit with the Toxin (3+) trait.

WING MEMBRANES

20 credits The Mutant automatically passes the Agility test to leap distances up to their Movement characteristic and when testing to jump down.

Если Out of Ammo также выпал на кубике огневой мощи, оружие заклинивает до конца боя., Damage (2)Раненая модель теряет X Wounds вместо одного. Если броска попадания нет (Template) — сначала D6, как выше.703

    A refractor field grants its wearer a 5+ Invulnerable save; however, should a natural 1 be rolled when making the Invulnerable save then the refractor field is burned out and cannot be used again for the rest of the battle.

    A refractor field may be combined with other armour and field armour.

PERSONAL EQUIPMENT

  • Bio-booster25 cr

    25 CREDITS – TP 0

    The first time in each battle that the bearer gains the Injured condition, reduce the Lethality characteristic of the weapon damaging them by 1. If the Lethality characteristic is now zero, roll 2 Injury dice instead of 1 and the bearer chooses which to apply; the other dice is discarded.

  • Drop rig10 cr

    10 CREDITS – TP 0

    An Active or Suppressed Fighter with a drop rig can perform the Descend action while they are within 1” of the edge of a platform:

    Descend (Single): The Fighter makes a move of up to 3” horizontally and up to 12” vertically. Any vertical movement must be downwards, i.e., towards the ground.

  • Medicae kit20 cr

    20 CREDITS – TP 0

    If a Fighter with a Medicare kit aids another Fighter’s Recovery test, they roll an additional Injury dice and choose which one to keep.

  • Photo-goggles35 cr

    35 CREDITS – TP 0

    A Fighter equipped with photo-goggle increases the value of X in the Visibility (X”) rule by 9” and may see through smoke clouds placed as part of the Smoke trait. Additionally, if a Fighter equipped with photo-goggles is hit by a weapon with the Flash trait, they suffer a -2 modifier to their Initiative check to avoid being blinded.

  • Photo-lumens15 cr

    15 CREDITS – TP 0

    Increase the value of X in the Visibility (X”) rule by 9” for this Fighter. This Fighter can always be targeted, regardless of the Visibility (X”) rule.

  • Respirator15 cr

    15 CREDITS – TP 0

    When a Fighter equipped with a respirator is hit by a weapon with the Gas trait, they gain a 5+ Invulnerable save against that weapon.

  • Stimm-slug stash25 cr

    25 CREDITS – TP 0

    Once per battle, a Fighter equipped with a stimm-slug stash may use it at the start of their activation. Until their next activation increase their Movement, Strength and Toughness characteristics by 2. At the start of their next activation, these effects wear off and the Fighter’s controller must roll a D6; on a 2+ nothing happens, but on a result of 1 they suffer a bad reaction to the stimms – they suffer a Str , AP -, L1 Hit that automatically wounds with no saves allowed.

WEAPON ACCESSORIES

  • Infra-sight10 cr

  • Las-projector20 cr

    20 CREDITS – TP 1

  • Mono-sight20 cr

GANG SPECIAL RULES

SPYRE HUNTING PARTY GANG COMPOSITION

Spyre Hunting Parties do not follow the usual gang composition rules in the Necromunda Skirmish Core Rulebook and instead have the following rule:

  • There must be one Fighter with the Leader Subtype.

If the Leader is ever deleted from the Gang Roster, follow the rule for Death of a Leader in the Necromunda Skirmish Core Rulebook.

INCOME, EQUIPMENT & RECRUITMENT

A Spyre Hunting Party gang gains control of Territories in the same way as a regular hang; they do not, however, gain the standard Boons from non-Spyrer Base Camp Territories they control; instead each non-Spyrer Base Camp Territory grants them the following Boon:

Income: The gang earns 15 credits from the Territory when collecting Income.

Spyre Hunter Fighters may freely put any weapons they are equipped with into the gang’s Stash and be equipped with new weapons during the Redistribute Equipment sub-step of the Post-cycle Sequence. Whenever a weapon is placed into the gang’s Stash, any Augmentations it may have gained are lost.

Additionally, Spyre Hunting Parties may not recruit any model that is not included in this list unless explicitly stated they will join Spyre Hunting Parties.

BASE OF OPERATIONS

Instead of starting with a Settlement Territory, a Spyre Hunting Party starts with a Spyrer Base Camp Territory which they can never lose.

UNIQUE TERRITORY -

SPYRER BASE CAMP

TERRITORY BOON

This Territory grants the following Boons:

Income: The gang earns 15 credits from this Territory when collecting income.

Special: At the start of each Post-cycle Sequence, one Spyrer may clear their In Recovery box before declaring Post-cycle Actions.

Scions of the Imperial House: Spyrers have a wide variety of rules that apply to them (see below).

Starting Skills: When added to a Gang Roster, all Spyre Hunting Party Leaders and Champions may select one skill from one of their Primary Skill Sets.

Skill Access: This gang’s Fighters have access to the following Skill Sets:
